name: Daily Mail cryptic crossword, book 2 No 96

book.title: Daily Mail New Cryptic Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Flower on the way to a life of pleasure

definitions.text: way to a life of pleasure

explanation.surface: A blossom spotted beside the road leading to an easy, pleasure-filled life.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'way' does double duty: it gives the second half of the wordplay and also ends the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, from Hamlet, describes the easy pursuit of pleasure, especially one leading to ruin.

clue.text: They take risks recklessly putting up rents

indicators.note: acting recklessly means without order or care, so the letters that follow are thrown about

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Landlords who keep raising rents are gambling with their tenants' goodwill.
explanation.definitionFit: Punters are gamblers, people who bet money and so take chances on an uncertain outcome.

clue.text: One pulling teeth away from the world?

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, while the answer is a noun phrase for a place of seclusion

blocks.note: ivories is slang for teeth, and tusks are ivory

explanation.surface: A dentist extracting teeth, supposedly detached from everyday reality.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a dentist, but 'One pulling' is one who tows, and the teeth are the material being pulled.
explanation.definitionFit: An ivory tower is a state of privileged seclusion from the practical concerns of ordinary life.

clue.text: Getting to the point of feeling pain again

explanation.surface: Someone nearly at the stage where an old pain returns.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving at a destination or stage is what someone does when they get there; the phrase means attaining it.

clue.text: Make sure about the dog being safe

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: to see to it that something happens
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: An owner checking that the dog is out of harm's way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something secure is protected from danger or harm, which is what being safe means.

clue.text: Engine knock when in perfect condition

blocks.note: first meaning: the rattling of a car engine from premature ignition
second meaning: the height of health

explanation.surface: A mechanic wondering why an engine in excellent shape still knocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinking is a noise from faulty combustion in petrol engines, and the pink means the very best state of health.

clue.text: Get a dog to go astray in a row

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
to err is to wander from the right path

explanation.surface: Advice on making a dog wander off down a line of houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a breed of small, lively dog originally used to hunt burrowing animals.

clue.text: Having fallen for dead bird during a good meal

definitions.note: describes a state after a fall, while the answer is a past participle meaning sprawled

indicators.note: something happening during an event falls within it, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a spread is a lavish meal

explanation.surface: Someone falling for a dead bird served up at a feast.
explanation.walkthrough: D and the bird go inside the meal, between its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying flat with arms and legs stretched out is the typical posture of someone who has fallen heavily.

clue.text: God followed by woman who couldn't keep a box shut

definitions.text: woman who couldn't keep a box shut

explanation.surface: A deity trailed by a notoriously curious woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woman' gives a name and also begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Pandora opened the jar or box given by Zeus, releasing all evils into mankind.

clue.text: Witch's spell able to cause a fall

explanation.surface: A sorceress's charm that can make people tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantrip is a Scots word for a charm or magic incantation cast by a witch.

clue.text: They write of the lamp going out in the Lords

indicators.note: going out suggests things falling apart or being dispersed, so the letters are rearranged
placed in something means set within it

blocks.note: members of the House of Lords are peers

explanation.surface: Writers describing a light being extinguished in the upper chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters sit after the first letter of the peers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pamphleteers are writers of short polemical booklets, so they are people who write.

clue.text: Her very wee twitch is seen all around

indicators.note: a twitch is a jerky movement, so the letters are jolted into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman's tiny nervous tic is noticed by everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean in every place or direction, throughout the whole surroundings.

clue.text: Being screened doesn't prevent it being seen

definitions.text: Being screened doesn't prevent it being seen

blocks.clueFragment: Being screened doesn't prevent it being seen
blocks.note: surface reading: something hidden behind a screen yet still visible
setter's reading: shown on a cinema screen, which is precisely how audiences watch it

explanation.walkthrough: Screened looks like concealed, but a movie is screened in the sense of projected, so screening is how it gets seen.
explanation.definitionFit: A movie is projected onto a cinema screen for audiences to watch it.

clue.text: She hopes to get money from that good old Australian

blocks.note: digger is slang for an Australian, especially a soldier

explanation.surface: A woman hoping to inherit money from a kindly elderly Australian.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold-digger is a person, usually a woman, who courts someone for their wealth.

clue.text: Take no notice of prompt payment reduction

blocks.note: second meaning: money knocked off a bill for paying quickly

explanation.surface: Ignore the offer of a lower price for paying on time.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to dismiss or disregard; as a noun it is a deduction from the usual price.

clue.text: He's keeping up with the German

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding something up makes it read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A man managing to keep pace with his German rival.
explanation.definitionFit: Tim is a man's name, so a male person referred to as he.

clue.text: One more to join a crowd?

definitions.text: One more to join a crowd?

blocks.clueFragment: One more to join a crowd?
blocks.note: surface reading: an extra person joining a throng
setter's reading: the saying that two's company, three's a crowd, so the next arrival is number four

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'two's company, three's a crowd' makes a crowd exactly three people.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinal for the person who comes after three others, making up a group of four.

clue.text: Trap for the spirit

blocks.note: first meaning: a snare for catching animals
second meaning: a juniper-flavoured alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A snare set to catch a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is an old word for a snare or noose, and also a clear distilled liquor.

clue.text: Russian turning up at the opening will find the way

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up flips the word so it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a gate is an opening in a wall or fence

explanation.surface: A Russian who arrives at the entrance will know the route.
explanation.definitionFit: To navigate is to plan and follow a route, so to work out how to get somewhere.

clue.text: Man worried about the song

indicators.note: worried in the sense of fretted or pulled about, so the letters are disturbed
about means around, so one piece encloses the next

explanation.surface: A man anxious about a particular tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a rousing song of praise or loyalty, such as a national one.

clue.text: Explorer of North America standing firm where there's smoke

definitions.note: a phrase pointing to the source of smoke, while the answer is a noun

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing upright makes a word read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: John Cabot explored the coast of North America in 1497

explanation.surface: A pioneer of the New World holding his ground amid smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Europeans first met tobacco in the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco is smoked in pipes and cigarettes, so it is found wherever smoke rises from a smoker.

clue.text: Bone of lamb Enid cooked

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A bone left over from the lamb that Enid roasted.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandible is the lower jawbone in mammals.

clue.text: Gets a fix and collapses

blocks.note: first meaning: fastens with a clasp
second meaning: gives way under pressure

explanation.surface: An addict gets a dose and then keels over.
explanation.definitionFit: To buckle is to fasten a belt or strap, and also to bend and give way under strain.

clue.text: Appear to find a heartless lady decent

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle part is removed

explanation.surface: Someone appears to discover a cold-hearted woman is respectable.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemly behaviour is proper and in good taste, conforming to accepted standards.

clue.text: Not quite the world in your ear

definitions.note: a locating phrase, while the answer is a noun for part of the ear

indicators.note: not quite complete means a letter is missing from the word

explanation.surface: A whisper that hints at something world-shaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The lobe is the soft lower part of the outer ear.

clue.text: One doesn't go all the way round

definitions.text: One doesn't go all the way round

blocks.clueFragment: One doesn't go all the way round
blocks.note: surface reading: someone who stops before completing a lap
setter's reading: a curved shape that covers only half of a full ring

explanation.definitionFit: It is a half of a round figure, so its arc stops at the diameter instead of closing.

clue.text: Some harness Martin's lost when there's a storm

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: a martingale is a strap of a horse's harness

explanation.surface: A horseman called Martin loses some tack in bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: A martingale is a strap from girth to noseband that stops a horse tossing its head; take away the name at its front.
explanation.definitionFit: A gale is a very strong wind, a storm.

clue.text: Speak of having to sort the mail after last month

indicators.note: sorting things moves them into a new order

explanation.surface: Complaining about sorting the Christmas post in the new year.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim is to speak aloud rhetorically, as in a formal recitation.

clue.text: Cornered for lack of grace

definitions.note: a phrase naming a quality, while the answer is an adjective for being bony and awkward

blocks.note: second meaning: bony and awkward, without soft curves

explanation.surface: Someone trapped because they were too clumsy to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Angular describes shapes with sharp angles, and figures or movements that are lean, stiff and ungainly.

clue.text: They seek relationships with no company to suit

blocks.note: one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Singles looking for love, with no partner to match them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonely hearts are single people who advertise for a romantic partner.
